edges.description: BAP31 bridges the ER and mitochondria through Tom40 and promotes import of the complex I subunit NDUFS4, so its loss is expected to lower complex I activity. The disease-level data are mixed and are recorded on the target node.
Liver enzyme elevation is attributed to BCAP31 loss because it occurs with intragenic variants and with every deletion that includes BCAP31; the hepatic mechanism is not known.

Proposed by the discovering authors from the white-matter phenotype and the known dependence of myelination on ER protein trafficking. No study has examined oligodendrocytes or myelin proteins in BAP31 deficiency.

edges.description: Proposed from a family with a BCAP31 in-frame insertion and nonsyndromic auditory neuropathy, whose lymphoblastoid cells showed mitochondrial dysfunction. It is an allelic phenotype, so its transfer to DDCH hearing loss is an inference. The cells were assayed for general mitochondrial dysfunction (ROS, ATP, membrane potential), not for complex I specifically, so drawing the edge from the complex I node is itself part of that inference.

nodes.description: BAP31-deficient patient fibroblasts are enlarged, with a swollen ER and a Golgi apparatus fragmented into scattered patches in up to about 30% of cells, and contain large vesicles with electron-dense inclusions. Constitutive BAP31 loss does not cause measurable accumulation of an ERAD substrate, activate the unfolded protein response, or trigger apoptosis, unlike transient knockdown, so the defect is placed in ER-to-Golgi exchange rather than in ER stress.

nodes.description: Reduced complex I activity was measured in cultured skin fibroblasts of one DDCH patient, and pleomorphic subsarcolemmal mitochondria were seen in another patient's muscle. Against this, respiratory-chain activities were normal in muscle of two patients and in fibroblasts of two brothers, and the mitochondrial network was normal in the founding patients' fibroblasts. The node is therefore a candidate mechanism, not an established one. The GO term is complex I assembly because the proposed route is BAP31-dependent import of the NDUFS4 subunit; the patient data measured complex I activity, not assembly.
